The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant/s - original claimant/s - legal heirs of the deceased - Babubhai, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 12.09.2006 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Ahmedabad (Rural) in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2009 of 1990, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.7,35,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponent No.2 liable to the extent 60% and opponents No.4 to 6 jointly and severally liable to the extent 40%, as it is a case of contributor negligence held by the Tribunal.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2009 of 1990,
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 That on 26.08.1990 at about 19:00 hours, deceased - Babubhai was travelling in Ambassador Car bearing registration No.GJ-3-9103 driven by the driver-cum-owner of the said car, in rash and negligent manner and by driving his car on totally wrong side, dashed with the Truck bearing registration No.PAT-299 coming from the opposite side.
Therefore, the claimants have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.12 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
It is noted that the claim NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined petition was filed by the widow and two minor children.
Thereafter, during pendency of the claim petition, widow has expired.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
None has appeared and contest the claim petition, except insurance companies of the Ambassador and Truck by disputing all the averments made by the claimant/s in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the claimant/s for enhancement.
3. Learned advocate Mr. P.M. Darji for the appellant/s - claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has submitted Amit Babubhai Mistry vs Jusubhai Sidikbhai Sumara (Deleted) on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151271051/
2

sentences.text: that amount of award is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined various aspects; like prospective income of the deceased, negligence, liability and family circumstances, etc.
He has submitted that the deceased was aged about only 37 years at the time of accident and was a furniture contractor and interior decorator.
He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his yearly income was Rs.75,000/-.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has not considered the prospective income of the deceased.
He has further submitted that the Tribunal has not properly considered the multiplier while awarding compensation.
He has fairly submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the income and deduction of personal expenses looking to the age of the deceased.

He has submitted that therefore, considering the loss of dependency, it would be calculated as Rs.75,000/- as yearly income plus 40% prospective income minus 1/3 as personal expenses multiplied by 15 multiplier would come to Rs.10,50,000/- total future loss, which should be awarded to the claimants by the learned Tribunal.
He has further submitted that considering the general and non-pecuniary damages, the learned Tribunal should award Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

He has also submitted that towards loss of consortium, there are three dependents and therefore, it should be awarded Rs.48,400/- to each dependent as per the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024
undefined decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has submitted that the compensation is required to be enhanced by modifying the award impugned accordingly and this appeal may be allowed.
4. Per contra, Mr. Palak Thakkar and Mr. Hemant Shah, learned advocates for respective respondents -
Insurance Companies have submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.

The Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased,
the age of the deceased, the dependency and future aspect of income.
They have submitted that under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation.
They have submitted that the amount under the head of loss of consortium is just and proper.
They have submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.

It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/08/2024 undefined object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
From the record, it transpires that the deceased was aged about 37 years and was a furniture contractor and interior decorator and his yearly income was Rs.75,000/- at the relevant point of time.
Therefore, it should be considered as yearly income of the deceased.

Hence, it would come to Rs.75,000/- per annum and by adding 40% prospective income, as not calculated by the learned Tribunal, it would come to Rs.30,000/- and therefore, total income comes to Rs1,05,000/-
per annum.

Since the deceased is aged about 37 years and there were three dependents, 1/3 would be proper to be deducted as personal expenses, which the Tribunal has rightly deducted and therefore, it would come to Rs.35,000/-.

Hence, the income NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined would come to Rs.70,000/- per annum and applying 15 multiplier as per the schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act as well as the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121

sentences.text: , it would come to Rs.10,50,000/- as future loss, which is required to be awarded to the claimants.

6.2 Further, considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), as general and non-pecuniary damages, under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, if we award Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/-, respectively, which would be the just and proper compensation.
6.3 Further, there are three dependents to the deceased.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, Rs.40,000/- consortium to each dependent and 10%
rise, which comes to Rs.48,400/- as consortium to each dependent, which total comes to Rs.1,45,200/-, which should be awarded to the claimants.

Therefore, I hold that the claimant/s are entitled to get the total amount of compensation of Rs.12,31,500/- with 9% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation,
which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.

The Tribunal has already awarded Rs.7,35,000/-, therefore, remaining amount of Rs.4,96,500/- would be the enhanced amount of compensation payable to the claimant/s.
8.
For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined
8.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.

8.2 Respondent No.6 - The United India Insurance Company Limited, which is the insurance company of the Truck, which has satisfied the basic award of the Tribunal, is directed to deposit the enhanced amount Rs.4,96,500/- with 9% p.a. interest from the date of claim petition till its realisation before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

8.3 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.

8.6 In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Khenyei versus New India Assurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/884/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined Limited reported in (2015) 9 SCC 273, it would be open for respondent No.6 - Insurance Company to recover the proportionate amount from the other tortfeasors, in accordance with law.
